ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists, OFAC SDN List, UK and EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, and New Zealand autonomous sanctions registers under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and the United Nations Act 1946. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) screening is performed in line with Sections 11-18 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Financial Markets Authority's 'AML/CFT Sector Risk Assessment—Beverage Franchising'. Enhanced due diligence (including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification) is mandatory where the UBO is a PEP, where funds originate from high-risk jurisdictions, or where sanctions-screening results are inconclusive. Screening is run at on-boarding, repeated on any material shareholding change, and re-run continuously via a licensed commercial screening database.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register (company name reservation and incorporation portal: https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Latin script. English and Māori names (including macronized Māori) are acceptable. Any non-Latin script must be transliterated into English characters. The legal name must end with 'Limited' or 'Tapui' (Māori for 'limited'). Names must not be identical or virtually identical to an existing company, must not contain a Restricted Name token without ministerial consent, and must not be misleading or offensive under Sections 20-22 of the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 20 working days from the date of reservation. If the proposed name is refused under ss 20-22 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may (i) submit a new reservation with a corrected or alternative name immediately, (ii) apply to the Registrar for re-determination attaching a written submission and supporting evidence (e.g., consent letter from a consenting entity or proof of distinctiveness), or (iii) request the prior written approval of the relevant regulatory ministry where a restricted token is involved. There is no dedicated statutory appeal tribunal for name refusals; the administrative fallback is an application to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972. Reservation extensions are not formally granted; an applicant may simply re-file the reservation (paying the applicable fee) while incorporation is being finalized, provided no third party has reserved the same name in the interim.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the registered office and director service address, provided the provider maintains a genuine physical street address in New Zealand at which legal documents can be served during statutory hours (Companies Act 1993, s 189). This is accepted for a franchise-licensing and syrups-supply-chain holding entity, subject to maintaining accessible corporate records in New Zealand. Registered agent and virtual office services are widely used by foreign-owned holding companies. The business requiring a physical operational location for inventory is not triggered at Stage 1 because the underlying New Zealand franchise operations and supply premises are separate local trading entities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-zero: approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a standard low-risk private franchise IP-holding company. The Companies Office does not routinely conduct physical site inspections, but Inland Revenue and the Financial Markets Authority may verify commercial substance, registered address accessibility, and local record-keeping if a tax, AML/CFT, or dormant-company risk flag is raised.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss 12–18 (incorporation), ss 20–22 and Sch 1 (constitution and default rules), ss 46–52 (share issues), ss 87–91 (registered office, records and minutes), ss 128–151 (directors and officers), and ss 214 and 318 (annual returns and removal); Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Income Tax Act 2007 (tax treatment); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (beneficial ownership due diligence)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a division of Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, operating the online Companies Register at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Companies Office online 'Register a Company' application (incorporation application) made under s 12 of the Companies Act 1993, together with the proposed constitution (if any), Form 2 consents-to-act of each director, subscriber share subscription statements, registered office address declaration, and payment of the prescribed registration fee
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists and no escrow account is required for an ordinary New Zealand limited liability company. The company must have at least one share and one shareholder, but the share capital may be nil paid, partly paid or fully paid in cash or non-cash consideration. However, the company must have at least one director resident in New Zealand or, if none, an eligible agent under s 10(2) of the Companies Act 1993; a separate physical registered office in New Zealand is mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [BOBA TEA GLOBAL FRANCHISE HOLDINGS LIMITED] (the 'Company'), PASSED AS AN UNANIMOUS RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS ON [DATE] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED: (1) That the application for incorporation be ratified and the Certificate of Incorporation be received as conclusive evidence of the Company's incorporation. (2) That the share capital be authorised for subscription and issued in accordance with the application for incorporation; that all subscription monies or other consideration be received and recorded in the share register; and that share certificates be issued accordingly. (3) That the registered office of the Company be adopted as [full physical street address, city, region, New Zealand], and that the directors be authorised to notify the Registrar of any future change. (4) That [Name(s)] be appointed as director(s) of the Company, and that [Name] be appointed as Company Secretary if required, each to hold office until resignation, removal or death, and to exercise the powers and duties set out in the Companies Act 1993. (5) That the directors be and are hereby authorised to open banking accounts in the name of the Company with a New Zealand registered bank, and to execute any signatory mandates and access the Company's bank accounts for the purposes of receiving franchise royalty wires and local POS settlements. (6) That the directors be authorised to apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number, GST registration, and any other tax registration required, and to register the Company on the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register. (7) That the directors be and are hereby authorised to negotiate, execute and deliver all leases, contracts, franchise agreements, supply chain agreements, trademark licenses, syndicate arrangements and other documents necessary to carry on the business of franchise licensing and boba tea syrup supply, subject always to the constitution and applicable New Zealand law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and name reservation on the New Zealand Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online register (register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a real-time search of the Companies Register and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and does not include a restricted or prohibited word under ss 22–24 of the Companies Act 1993. The name must end with 'Limited' unless an exemption under s 24 applies for a non-resident or overseas company. Reserve the name online through the Companies Office incorporation portal; the system immediately validates availability and flags restricted terms. If a restricted word or expression is used, attach the written consent of the relevant Minister or statutory body. For this franchise entity, a name such as 'Boba Tea Global Franchise Holdings NZ Limited' is recommended. No notarisation is required at this stage, but due diligence records for the proposed directors and shareholders must be collected for subsequent AML/CFT compliance.
required_dossiers: Proposed full company name and two alternative names
Passport or national identity document for each proposed director and shareholder
Proof of residential address for each director and shareholder (issued within the last 3 months)
Proposed registered office physical street address (not a P.O. Box)
Written consents from any holders of restricted words (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because of similarity or likelihood of deception, the applicant may submit another name immediately. The applicant may also apply to the Registrar for discretionary approval under s 24 Companies Act 1993 with supporting evidence, or seek an order in the High Court for determination of the entitlement to the name. The Companies Office will issue a requisition identifying the objection, and the applicant has 10 working days to respond or propose an alternative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of constitutional documents, share subscription plan, and officer consent instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders / New Zealand legal representative or corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution under s 26 of the Companies Act 1993, or elect that Schedule 1 of the Act applies. The constitution should stipulate the share classes, restrictions on share transfers, board quorum and voting procedures, director indemnification provisions, capital adjustment mechanisms, and dividend policy, aligning with the 'International Company' holding structure and franchise royalty pipeline. The subscriber shareholders sign a share subscription schedule indicating the classes and numbers of shares to be issued, whether fully paid, partly paid or unpaid, and the consideration to be paid in cash or kind. Each proposed director signs a consent-to-act form in accordance with s 150 of the Act, confirming their capacity and availability to act. The registered office address must be a physical street address in New Zealand, and if the office is not owned by the company, the occupant must provide a letter of consent. For tax-exempt offshore income planning, obtain a written opinion from New Zealand tax counsel confirming eligibility for the applicable foreign branch exemption or international tax concession, and ensure the constitution is silent on any prohibited activities.
required_dossiers: Constitution (original or certified copy, signed by all shareholders)
Shareholders' subscription schedule and share class designations
Directors' consent-to-act form (Form 2)
Shareholder resolution for approval of the constitution (if not adopting default Schedule 1 rules)
Registered office address and occupant's written consent
Evidence of directors' New Zealand physical presence or executed agency agreement under s 10 Companies Act 1993
Tax structure memorandum and beneficial ownership register draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the constitution is defective or inconsistent with the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar will issue a notice requiring revision before registration; the board may simply rely on the Schedule 1 default constitution in the interim. If a director's consent is later found to be forged or defective, the appointment is void ab initio and the company must rectify the register by a new consent and an application to the High Court for correction of the Companies Register under s 91 Companies Act 1993, or by re-filing with the Companies Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application and payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online portal: www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the 'New company incorporation' application on the Companies Office website, entering all shareholder and director details, the registered office and electronic mailing address, capital allotment and the ANZSIC/industry classification code (e.g., H4512 Food and Beverage Service, or L6911 Franchising). Attach the constitution, the signed Form 2 consents, the registered office address consent, and any supporting consents for restricted names. The authorised applicant—the director, shareholder or a licensed agent—signs the application electronically using RealMe identity verification or the company's digital sign-in. Pay the fee of NZD 120.00 (approximately USD 74.00) online; this includes one integrated GST and fee charge. After submission, the Registrar will perform an automated name and statutory data check and may manually review if the application is for a high-risk jurisdiction or includes restricted phrases. Once satisfied, the Registrar enters the company onto the Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed NZ Companies Office online incorporation form with application reference
Constitution (if any)
Directors' consent-to-act (Form 2) for each director
Registered office address declaration and landlord consent (if third party)
Shareholder beneficial ownership and AML/CFT identity verification pack
Power of attorney or signed engagement letter if filing through a corporate agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or returned under s 17 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant is notified of the specific requisition and is given 10 working days to supply further information or correct the document; pending resolution, no additional fee is payable for a genuine correction. If the Registrar gives a final refusal, the applicant may request an internal review and thereafter apply to the High Court by way of judicial review. If rejection arises from a name dispute, the applicant may simultaneously file a new application with a dissimilar name and pursue legal rights under s 22.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation statutory and revenue registrations (NZBN, IRD, GST, FIC, and Companies Office annual return setup)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD); New Zealand Companies Office / NZBN Registrar; Department of Internal Affairs (for AML/CFT supervision)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, the Companies Office automatically issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) which acts as the company's unique identifier. Within 10 working days of incorporation, apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number using the online myIR service, or file the IR596 form. The application should disclose directors' IRD status (resident/non-resident) and provide the corporate shareholding, record date and intended business activity. If the company expects annual gross revenue to exceed NZD 60,000, it must apply for GST registration; the franchise royalty wires and local POS settlement income will be assessable and GST treatment depends on whether the recipient is an overseas recipient. The company must also file its first beneficial ownership return with the Companies Office under the anti-money laundering regime, declaring each person who holds or controls 25% or more of the company's shares or voting rights. Additionally, instruct the bank onboarding team (with the AML/KYC dossier) to open the operating bank account for receipt of franchise royalties and local POS settlements. Finally, set up the annual return calendar on the Companies Register so that the s 214 annual return is lodged each anniversary.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation letter from Companies Office
Form IR596 (IRD number application for companies)
GST registration application (Form IR322 or online)
Beneficial ownership register and shareholder identification documents
AML/KYC compliance pack for corporate bank account
Completed trustee/foreign company information schedules, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD processing is delayed or queried for missing non-resident shareholder information, the IRD may issue a notice requiring the entity to obtain an IRD number; an extension may be sought under the Tax Administration Act 1994 if the information is genuinely unavailable from the overseas parent. For late registration or filing, the company may voluntarily disclose to reduce penalties and apply for remission under s 183A of the Tax Administration Act 1994. If the beneficial ownership filing is rejected, re-file the corrected return online; a default will not prevent the annual return if the error is technical and the Companies Office allows correction under s 91.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government; online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myIR)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity engaging in New Zealand tax-affected activities must apply for an IRD number using the Non-Resident Companies IRD Number application. The application requires completion of form IR742 (Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application) or registration through myIR where eligibility exists, supported by certified constitutive documents (Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association), evidence of foreign tax residence, and details of the New Zealand resident agent or tax representative if the company is not carrying on a taxable activity but has New Zealand-sourced income. For VAT/GST purposes, registration is effected separately under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 using form GST1 (for non-resident businesses) where the non-resident carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand or makes supplies in the course of that activity. Compulsory registration applies to any person carrying on a taxable activity whose total value of supplies in a 12-month period exceeds or is expected to exceed NZD 60,000; non-resident suppliers of remote services (including digital services, franchise royalties, and licensing fees) are subject to the offshore supplier registration regime under section 60(1B) of the GST Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: A Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) is a tax-exempt offshore entity under the Cook Islands International Companies Act 1981-82; it is resident for tax purposes in the Cook Islands only if its management and control is exercised there, and if it obtains a tax exemption certificate it is exempt from Cook Islands tax on foreign-sourced income. For New Zealand tax purposes, the entity is treated as a non-resident company under the Income Tax Act 2007 unless it has a fixed establishment in New Zealand and derives New Zealand-sourced business income. The CK_IC will be classified as a foreign company with entity-level tax treatment in New Zealand only to the extent it derives New Zealand-sourced income that is not exempt under a Double Tax Agreement or the residual non-resident withholding tax regime; no New Zealand pass-through eligibility applies, and the entity is outside the New Zealand look-through company (LTC) and partnership regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: (1) New Zealand GST registration election for non-resident suppliers of remote services under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to register and charge GST on a reverse-charge basis where the recipient is a non-resident; (2) election to use the special GST margin scheme for secondhand goods, not applicable to franchise business; (3) election under section FC 17 of the Income Tax Act 2007 for a foreign company to file a New Zealand return and claim deductions against New Zealand-sourced income; (4) hybrid mismatch election mechanisms under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018, including the ability to elect to align tax treatment of the CK_IC with New Zealand entity treatment for a controlled foreign company (CFC) or foreign branch where applicable, subject to the OECD hybrid mismatch rules; (5) no check-the-box election equivalent exists under New Zealand tax law; the CK_IC should instead rely on the CFC attribution rules and the branch equivalent test for foreign entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (New Zealand value-added tax regime, including the offshore supplier registration regime)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration threshold: NZD 60,000 (total value of taxable supplies in any 12-month period, or expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in the following 12 months, for a person carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand). Non-resident offshore suppliers of remote services (e.g., franchise royalties, digital platform services, licensing of syrups formulations) are required to register and charge GST on supplies made to non-resident recipients residing in New Zealand once their total supplies to New Zealand-resident customers exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period. Voluntary registration is available to non-residents even below the threshold where the person carries on a taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction controls regime. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and governed by the GST Act 1985 and Inland Revenue guidelines; e-invoices must contain all prescribed tax invoice details (supplier name, GST number, invoice date, description, amount, GST amount, and zero-rating statement where applicable). The New Zealand Tax Invoice and e-Invoicing framework aligns with the Peppol network; registration on the Peppol Business Interoperability Framework is optional. There is no statutory requirement for digital stamping, fiscal API integration, or pre-clearance approval from Inland Revenue before invoice issuance. However, a registered person must issue a tax invoice within 5 working days of a recipient's request, and DEAR or other accounting systems must be capable of producing full GST-compliant tax invoices and GST return filings via myIR.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from New Zealand are zero-rated for GST where the supplier removes the goods from New Zealand within 28 days after supply and supplies them to a recipient who is outside New Zealand, in accordance with section 11(1)(a) and section 11(2)(a) of the GST Act 1985. The supply of services (including franchise licensing, royalty payments, and the supply of a business or part thereof) is zero-rated where the services are performed for a person who is non-resident and not in New Zealand when the services are performed, and the services are supplied in the course of the supplier's taxable activity (section 11A(1)(a)). The CK_IC exporting syrups and beverage formulations from New Zealand to international franchisees must retain contemporaneous documentary evidence proving physical export, including the Customs Export Declaration. Zero-rating for offshore supplies of intellectual property and franchise rights also applies to non-resident recipients, but where the supply is deemed to be a supply of services that is connected with New Zealand land or goods situated in New Zealand at the time of supply, domestic GST at 15% applies. Zero-rating is also denied for services physically performed in New Zealand where the benefit is enjoyed in New Zealand, and for supplies to non-resident business recipients who are GST-registered in New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export declaration lodged via New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window or approved EDI provider, including customs tariff classification and statistical value)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (showing exporter as CK_IC or its New Zealand operating subsidiary, consignee overseas, and port of loading in New Zealand)

Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Confirmation of Export Proceeds (IRD and Customs may require evidence of foreign exchange repatriation into a New Zealand bank account or the CK_IC's offshore bank account for export payment reconciliation)
Proof of export and supplier-issued GST tax invoice (zero-rated supply statement with delivery terms and incoterms)
Packing list and certificate of origin (if applicable for preferential duty treatment)
Shipping contract or insurance certificate (where relevant to evidence movement of goods)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand Inland Revenue and New Zealand Customs Service undertake joint audit scrutiny of export zero-rating claims. Where a taxpayer incorrectly zero-rates a domestic supply or fails to retain the required export documentation, the GST output tax is retrospectively clawed back and assessed as a shortfall in GST payable, with interest pursuant to section 107 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, plus a shortfall penalty of 20% for an unacceptable tax position (or 40% where gross carelessness or an abusive tax position is established). Knowingly or recklessly lodging a false GST return with an intention to evade GST is a criminal offence under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, carrying a maximum fine of NZD 50,000 for the first offence and NZD 100,000 for subsequent offences, as well as a possible term of imprisonment under section 143A(2)(e). Anti-money laundering countermeasures under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 require banks to furnish transaction records; any false export documentation or circular trading patterns for fraudulent zero-rating may trigger a report to the Financial Intelligence Unit, and the New Zealand Customs Service may impose penalties under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 of up to NZD 10,000 per false declaration and forfeiture of goods.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return of Corporate Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (Realm of New Zealand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three calendar months after each anniversary of incorporation; filed through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 100; registered agent must give cessation notice after 30 days of unpaid fees; continued default for three months triggers administrative strike-off and vesting of assets in the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Shareholding Transfer Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (via licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted concurrently with the annual return, within three months after the anniversary of incorporation; any shareholding transfer is declared immediately upon registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 10,000 under the Beneficial Ownership (Information) Act 2017 for non-filing or false filing; inaccurate confirmation suspends the certificate of good standing and may lead to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Annual Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent and Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; renewal confirmation is lodged with the annual return within three months of that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of the registered agent opens a 60-day replacement window; failure to appoint a replacement results in administrative strike-off proceedings by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applies to a Cook Islands International Company; an independent audit is triggered only where the constitutional documents require it, the Financial Supervisory Commission issues a corrective AML/CFT direction, or a consolidated reporting parent exceeds New Zealand large-company thresholds (revenue above NZD 30 million or total assets above NZD 60 million).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP is accepted for internal and lender-facing records; no public financial statement filing obligation applies under Cook Islands law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent maintains the beneficial ownership register and files the annual confirmation with the annual return; every shareholding transfer is declared immediately with completed KYC documentation, and the statutory registers are updated at the registered office before the next annual confirmation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (New Zealand resident company rate, Income Tax Act 2007, Sch 1 Part B). The CK_IC (Cook Islands International Company) is tax-exempt in the Cook Islands (0% CIT on offshore income) and is treated as a non-resident company in New Zealand; NZ tax exposure is limited to NZ-sourced income (royalties, syrup sales with source in NZ, and income attributable to a NZ fixed establishment).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays in New Zealand. Applicable reliefs: (1) R&D tax incentive - 15% refundable tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure (caution: royalty/IP exploitation activity generally not eligible); (2) indefinite loss carry-forward subject to 49% shareholder continuity; (3) non-resident IC exemption for foreign-sourced income and for royalties/interest subject to final Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT); (4) no New Zealand capital gains tax on disposal of shares or franchise assets outside an income account; (5) Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% may substitute for NRWT on certain registered public-issue interest.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited - no statutory 5-year cap under New Zealand law (subject to 49% continuity of shareholding); the CK_IC, as a tax-exempt non-resident with no NZ trading PE, ordinarily has no NZ tax loss pool to carry forward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (residential company income tax return) / IR4NZ (non-resident company income tax return), filed electronically through the Inland Revenue 'myIR' secure online portal or via approved tax agent software. The CK_IC files IR4NZ only if it derives assessable NZ-source income through a fixed establishment; otherwise its NZ franchise royalties are subject to final NRWT withholding by the NZ payer and no return is required for those amounts.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; provisional tax in 3 instalments for standard 31 March balance dates (28 August, 15 January, 7 May) or 6 instalments for GST-registered 6-monthly filers; terminal tax due 7 February (non-agent) or 7 April (tax agent extension).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance date: return due 7 July of the same calendar year (agent extension: 31 March of the following year); terminal tax due 7 February (agent: 7 April). For non-standard balance dates, the return is due on the 7th day of the 4th month after balance date and terminal tax on the 7th day of the 7th month after balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4/IR4NZ Box 1 - Entity name and IRD number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the company as registered, postal address, and New Zealand IRD number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact Cook Islands registered name of the CK_IC. If no NZ IRD number exists, apply for non-resident registration (IR 596) before lodging. Overseas addresses are acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4/IR4NZ Box 2 - Balance date and tax year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standard NZ tax year end. A non-resident IC with no PE must still observe the NZ rule for any withholding certificates attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income included in assessable income for the NZ tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: report only NZ-sourced income, e.g. gross proceeds from syrup concentrate sales sourced in NZ and NZ business income attributable to a fixed establishment. Exclude offshore franchise royalties not sourced in NZ. For the CK_IC, NZ franchise royalties are generally subject to final NRWT and are not re-returned here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses incurred in deriving assessable income under s DA 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only arm's length expenses directly related to NZ-source income. Apportion head-office overhead using an acceptable OECD method if mixed; no deduction is available for foreign-sourced or exempt income expenditures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4/IR4NZ Box 7 - Net profit or loss before loss offsets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for tax (add-backs, deductibility disallowances).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC, ensure depreciation, amortisation and TP adjustments are made in accordance with NZ tax rules and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4/IR4NZ Box 10 - Net taxable income or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying loss carry-forwards and group loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss continuity (49% same-ownership test) applies. A non-resident IC that has never filed an NZ return cannot utilise prior losses without evidence of assessment history.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4 Box 12 / IR4NZ Box 11 - Income tax on taxable income at 28%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of corporate income tax at 28% on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident companies pay 28%. A non-resident IC with a NZ PE pays 28% on NZ-attributable income, with NRWT credits offset. Royalties not attributable to a PE are excluded from this calculation because final NRWT has already discharged the income tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4 Box 14 / IR4NZ Box 13 - Total tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for resident withholding tax, NRWT, imputation credits, PAYE tax credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach copies of NRWT deduction summaries (IR 66) and any NZ interest/dividend withholding certificates. Foreign tax credits are generally unavailable to a tax-exempt IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4 Box 19 / IR4NZ Box 15 - Terminal tax or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balancing payment or refund after deducting provisional tax and credits from tax on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If NRWT withheld exceeds the 28% liability on PE profits, claim the excess by filing the return and supporting schedules; refunds are paid by direct credit to the non-resident bank account after verification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: NZD 250 immediate penalty plus NZD 50 for each month the return is overdue (capped at NZD 500 per company). Late payment: 1% penalty on the day after due date, 4% penalty on day 8, then 1% per month thereafter. Use of Money Interest (UOMI) accrues on underpaid tax from the due date to payment date (current underpaid rate approximately 9.7% - 10.7% p.a., reset quarterly). The Commissioner may issue a default assessment, cancel loss carry-forwards, and initiate debt collection (bank attachment, court judgment, and departure prohibition order).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory NRWT on dividends to non-residents: 30% (Income Tax Act 2007, Sch 3). Treaty reduced rates: generally 15% for portfolio dividends; 5% for fully imputed dividends to a 10% corporate shareholder under the NZ-Australia DTA; 15% for most other comprehensive DTAs. The Cook Islands has no comprehensive DTA with New Zealand, so dividends paid from the NZ operating entity to the CK_IC attract the full 30% NRWT, subject to imputation credits reducing the economic burden where the NZ payer attaches credits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (1) The non-resident recipient obtains a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of its residence jurisdiction. (2) The recipient provides the TRC, together with a signed declaration of beneficial ownership, to the NZ withholding agent before payment. (3) The NZ payer applies the reduced treaty rate at source and retains the TRC on file (IRD's NRWT guidance, IR 290 series). (4) If over-withheld, the non-resident must file an IR 67 (Non-Resident Withholding Tax return) with the IRD within the statutory claim period (generally 12 months from the end of the income year) to obtain a refund. (5) TRCs must be renewed annually and upon any change of circumstances; absence of a TRC means the statutory 30% dividend / 15% royalty / 15% interest rate applies. For the CK_IC, no treaty relief exists on NZ-Cook Islands flows; the revenue authority of the Cook Islands does not issue NZ-recognised TRCs for NRWT reduction purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties from franchisees to the CK_IC: statutory NRWT at 15% on royalties derived from New Zealand (s RF 2 and Sch 3, ITA 2007). Treaty rates vary: Australia 5%, US 5%, China 10%, Singapore 10%, UK 10%. The Cook Islands has no DTA, so the CK_IC bears a final 15% NRWT on NZ franchise royalty wires. Interest on intercompany loans from the CK_IC to the NZ operating company: statutory NRWT 15%; treaty rates commonly 10% (US, China, UK) and 10% under NZ-Australia DTA; AIL at 2% may substitute for NRWT where the debtor is an approved issuer and the interest is on registered securities quoted on an exchange. The CK_IC, being in a non-treaty jurisdiction, is ineligible for treaty-reduced interest rates and must rely on AIL only where the borrower makes the approved issuer election.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory contemporaneous documentation where aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 1,000,000 in an income year (general goods/services/intangibles) or NZD 3,000,000 for related-party interest/financial transactions. Master File and Country-by-Country Report: mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least NZD 1,150,000,000 (EUR 750,000,000 equivalent). The CK_IC franchise and syrup supply structure must maintain transfer pricing documentation even below the NZD 1m threshold where the IRD's risk assessment identifies unclear pricing, excessive royalty rates or loss-making NZ franchise entities.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no codified 'Economic Substance Regulations' statute analogous to the UAE/BVI/Cayman regimes. However, the CK_IC must demonstrate real economic substance under: (1) the NZ General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s BG 1, ITA 2007) which recharacterises tax avoidance arrangements where the IC lacks commercial reality; (2) ss GC 13-14 transfer pricing rules requiring the actual allocation of functions, assets and risks (OECD DEMPE analysis) - the IC must own, develop, enhance and manage the boba tea IP and syrup formulation; (3) the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test (PPT) where treaty benefits are sought - unavailable to the Cook Islands IC but relevant to any chain using a treaty-resident intermediary; (4) NZ thin capitalisation rules (s FE 4) limiting interest deductibility in the NZ borrower to a 60% debt-to-asset safe harbour where the CK_IC lends to the NZ entity; (5) the Indefeasible Anti-Money Laundering / Know-Your-Customer framework (AML/CFT Act 2009) requiring beneficial ownership and substance verification of the IC by NZ banks and franchisees. Practical substance for the IC: registered office, local corporate secretary, at least two resident directors, board meeting minutes of genuine IP/DEMPE decisions, a substantive IP register, royalty benchmarking study, and a material intercompany agreement with contemporaneous documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Offence (s 143A, Tax Administration Act 1994)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting franchise royalty income or syrup supply proceeds from NZ tax filings (IR4/IR4NZ); creating fictitious supplier invoices from shell companies to strip profit from the NZ franchise entity; backdating franchise agreements; destroying or falsifying records of royalty wire transfers and local POS trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction: fine up to NZD 250,000 for a company and imprisonment for up to 5 years (for individuals involved); civil shortfall penalty of 100% of the evaded tax (s 141E); re-assessment with the 4-year time bar extended indefinitely for evasion; UOMI and late payment penalties apply; restraint and forfeiture of assets under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are treated as principals: personal fines up to NZD 50,000 per offence and imprisonment up to 5 years. Directors of the NZ borrower/franchise entity are personally liable for unpaid withholding taxes (PAYE/RWT/NRWT) under s 172-174 TAA; fraudulent trading liability under s 300 Companies Act 1993 for debts; departure prohibition orders (travel bans) may be issued under s 174B TAA for serious tax debt; disqualification from directorship up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance (s BG 1 GAAR / OECD MLI PPT / AML/CFT Act 2009)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The CK_IC operates with no physical presence, no employees, no genuine board meetings, no bank account in its own name, and no DEMPE substance while receiving high-margin royalty streams from NZ franchisees; using the Cook Islands OECD-white-listed jurisdiction and the NZ brand origin reputation solely as a tax shield; failure of the NZ franchisee and banks to perform beneficial ownership verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may cancel tax benefits retrospectively and reconstruct the transactions: royalty and syrup payments recharacterised as dividends to the real controllers or re-attributed to the NZ trading entity; additional tax at 28% on the reassessed profit; shortfall penalties: 20% for unacceptable tax positions, 40% for abusive tax positions (s 141D); 100% penalty where evasion is proven; reversal of NRWT offsets; cancellation of any treaty claim; the AML/CFT supervisor may impose a civil penalty up to NZD 2 million for reporting entities failing CDD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors holding the ultimate economic interest cannot hide behind the corporate veil: joint and several liability for the company's tax debt under GAAR reconstructions; personal exposure for reckless trading (s 135 Companies Act 1993); adverse findings by banks automatically trigger account termination and reporting to the NZ Financial Intelligence Unit; travel bans under departure prohibition orders; disqualification and potential extradition proceedings where fraud is suspected.
